# Configtree Requirements Checklist: Import and Fast Merge

**Purpose**: Review the clarity, completeness, and consistency of the Configtree Import, Merge, metadata, and revision lifecycle requirements before task generation.
**Created**: 2026-10-12
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by `$speckit-checklist` from the feature specification and [plan](../plan.md).
**Review Ownership**: This is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines that the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` records approval of requirements quality; it does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are the accepted file formats, document roots, filename prefixes, and multi-file combination rules all specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002–FR-004]
- [x] CHK002 Are the exact metadata-wrapper recognition rules and the treatment of ordinary mappings specified together? [Completeness, Spec §FR-020–FR-021]
- [x] CHK003 Are the rules for associating extracted metadata with flattened content paths specified, including paths without an exact match? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK004 Are the supported direct edits to the pending key-value dictionary, its lifetime, and the meaning of pending removal specified? [Completeness, Spec §FR-023–FR-025]
- [x] CHK005 Are the required stages and ordering of revision creation, batch storage, optional commit, and head selection documented for both workflows? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005–FR-006, §FR-013, §FR-017, §FR-024]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK006 Is it unambiguous that a metadata wrapper requires exactly `value` and dictionary-valued `metadata`, including an empty dictionary? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK007 Is the difference between splitting metadata and flattening a wrapped mapping value clear, including the rule against metadata inheritance? [Clarity, Spec §FR-021–FR-022]
- [x] CHK008 Is the expected representation of strings, non-string leaf values, lists, empty objects, and dates clear enough to distinguish content from metadata? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, §FR-014, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK009 Is the exposed dictionary clearly defined as one live pending collection, including what users may change and when those changes become final? [Clarity, Spec §FR-017, §FR-023]
- [x] CHK010 Is the meaning of “one batch” precise for nonempty, empty, aborted, and invalid pending dictionaries? [Clarity, Spec §FR-024–FR-025, §SC-010]
- [x] CHK011 Are the four parts of a parsed refspec, scope meaning, and revision-versus-milestone classification unambiguous? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008–FR-010]
- [x] CHK012 Is “fast merge” defined through concrete key retention, addition, and conflict criteria rather than an implied revision-history rule? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012–FR-015, Assumptions]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK013 Do the wrapper examples, prose rules, and Import acceptance scenarios agree on falsy values, empty metadata, and mappings with extra fields? [Consistency, Spec §Metadata Splitting Rules, User Story 1]
- [x] CHK014 Do the exact-path metadata rule and the promised preservation of imported leaf values agree for wrapped mapping values? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, §FR-022, §SC-001, §SC-008]
- [x] CHK015 Is pending-entry removal consistently distinguished from deleting an inherited or previously stored key? [Consistency, Spec §FR-023–FR-025, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK016 Do the batch-count requirements distinguish a submitted batch from a completed successful workflow when storage or commit fails? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016–FR-017, §FR-024, §SC-010]
- [x] CHK017 Are source and destination scope rules consistent across refspec parsing, Merge, and synchronous/asynchronous parity requirements? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §FR-008–FR-011, §FR-018]
- [x] CHK018 Are the stricter final-entry validity rules in the design reconciled with the specification's promise to use existing key-value contracts? [Conflict, Spec §FR-025, Plan §Validation and compatibility]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK019 Can every combination of Import commit and head-update choices be evaluated from a stated revision status and head-selection outcome? [Measurability, Spec §FR-006, §SC-002]
- [x] CHK020 Are the expected imported paths and metadata attachments specific enough to judge the mixed-format and wrapper scenarios objectively? [Measurability, Spec §User Story 1, §Metadata Splitting Rules, §SC-001, §SC-008]
- [x] CHK021 Are the expected results for compatible and conflicting merges measurable in terms of retained keys, reported conflicts, revisions, and heads? [Measurability, Spec §FR-012–FR-015, §SC-004–SC-005]
- [x] CHK022 Are the criteria for dictionary edit visibility, final contents, and zero or one batch submission stated with observable limits? [Measurability, Spec §User Story 3, §SC-009–SC-010]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK023 Are primary Import and Merge flows independently specified for both synchronous and asynchronous callers? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories 1–2, §FR-001]
- [x] CHK024 Are alternate flows for milestone, explicit revision, head selection, same-tree merge, and empty-key revisions covered? [Coverage, Spec §FR-006, §FR-010–FR-013, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK025 Are body exceptions, validation failures, storage failures, commit failures, and head-update failures each covered by stated publication and recovery requirements? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 4, §FR-007, §FR-016–FR-017, §FR-025]
- [x] CHK026 Are asynchronous cancellation requirements stated for all stages where a revision might already exist and a later publication step might otherwise start? [Coverage, Spec §FR-007, §FR-016, §FR-018, §SC-006]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK027 Are missing/empty files, duplicate filename stems, duplicate or ambiguous content paths, and unsupported document values addressed before revision creation? [Coverage, Spec §FR-003–FR-004, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK028 Are wrapper-shaped list elements, document-root wrappers, nested wrapped mappings, null metadata, and metadata names containing slashes addressed explicitly? [Coverage, Spec §FR-020–FR-022, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK029 Are absent metadata and explicit `{}` treated consistently in Import, editable entries, and Merge conflict rules? [Coverage, Spec §FR-012, §FR-020, §FR-023, Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK030 Are invalid refspec components, missing heads, absent key data, and zero or multiple milestone matches covered, including matches across result pages? [Coverage, Spec §FR-008–FR-011, Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK031 Is the one-batch performance objective bounded by a documented outcome for payloads that exceed existing platform request limits? [Gap, Spec §FR-024, Plan §Technical Context]
- [x] CHK032 Are the consistency limits of concurrent head changes and edits made during finalization documented where users could infer stronger publication guarantees? [Gap, Spec §FR-011, §FR-023, Plan §Validation and compatibility]
- [x] CHK033 Are requirements for safe document interpretation, error detail, and protection of imported content in failure messages sufficiently explicit for this configuration workflow? [Gap, Spec §FR-003, §FR-016, Plan §Phase 1: Design]

## Dependencies, Assumptions, and Ambiguities

- [x] CHK034 Are the assumptions about authentication, existing trees, committed parent revisions, and platform inheritance stated alongside their effect on Import and Merge? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-011, Plan §Validation and compatibility]
- [x] CHK035 Is the required behavior clear when a user edits an encoded value in the public dictionary without updating its related payload fields? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-023–FR-025, Plan §Validation and compatibility]
- [x] CHK036 Are the no-retry/no-rollback assumption and recoverable revision ID/stage requirements consistent for uncertain remote completion and asynchronous cancellation? [Assumption, Spec §FR-007, §FR-016, §SC-006]

## Notes

- This checklist covers requirements writing for a PR reviewer at standard depth. Its strongest focus is rio-compatible metadata splitting and the editable pending dictionary with one batch submission. Import, Merge, execution-mode parity, and failure recovery are included where they affect those contracts.
- Items carrying `[Gap]`, `[Ambiguity]`, or `[Conflict]` invite the reviewer to judge whether the current specification already resolves the concern or needs refinement. They are not assertions that the implementation fails.
- Mark items `[x]` only after reviewing the specification and related design artifacts. Leave items unchecked when their requirements-quality criteria still need clarification or correction.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify reviewer markers. `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
